info.title: DNS as a Service
info.description:
EdgeЦентр provides an API that allows you to interact with DNSaaS.

DNSaaS allows for managing DNS zones and records.

# Overview

Our API has resource-oriented, predictable URLs and uses the HTTP response codes to indicate API errors.
We use standard HTTP features, such as HTTP authentication and HTTP terminology, that HTTP clients can understand.
JSON is returned in all API responses, including errors.

### Maximum body request

Maximum API body request size is 1MB.

### Rate limits

There is a general limit of 4 requests per second. If you go over the rate limit, you will receive a response status of 429.

tags.name: RRsets
tags.description:
Manages your RRsets. RRsets can be either static or dynamic.
  • Static RRsets are those that have no response selection filters enabled.
  • Dynamic RRsets are those that have one or more response selection filters enabled.
    •  With dynamic RRsets, the resource records are selected for DNS response based on their metadata, applied filters, and the __strict__ field value. ### Strict field If `strict: true`, then only records matching the filter are returned in the response. If none match the filter, no records are returned. If `strict: false`, then all records are returned in the response if no records match the filter. ### Metadata The following metadata can be added to the resource records:
  • ip — a list of network addresses in CIDR format
    • Example: `meta: {ip: [92.101.12.150/25]}` or `meta: {ip: [1024:de:1010::/48]}`
  • asn — a list of autonomous system numbers
    • Example: `meta: {asn: 12345}` or `meta: {asn: 67890}`
  • regions — a list of country region codes. We use the ISO 3166-2 format to specify the region for all countries except Russia. To specify the region of Russia, use the data according to GOST 7.67. Use the following format to specify Russian regions that do not have codes in GOST 7.67:
    • `ru-sev` — Sevastopol
    • `ru-cri` — Crimea
    • `ru-don` — DNR
    • `ru-lug` — LNR
    • `ru-zap` — Zaporozhye
    • `ru-khe` — Kherson
    • Example: `meta: {regions: [ru-kya]}` or `meta: {regions: [ru-mow]}`
  • countries — a list of country codes
    • Example: `meta: {countries: [kz]}` or `meta: {countries: [am]}`
  • continents — a list of continent codes
    • Example: `meta: {continents: [eu]}` or `meta: {continents: [as]}`
  • latlong — latitude and longitude coordinates
    • Example: `meta: {latlong: [-37.813755, 144.962672]}` or `meta: {latlong: [34.056152, -118.247055]}`
  • weight — the weight of the resource record from 0 to 100
    • Example: `meta: {weight: 10}` or `meta: {weight: 50}`
  • default — determines, if the resource record should be used by default when other records are not selected based on their meta
    • Example: `meta: {default: true}` or `meta: {default: false}`
  • backup — determines, if the resource record should be included in the response only when DNS Failover detects the outage of all non-backup records
    • Example: `meta: {backup: true}` or `meta: {backup: false}`
  • notes — any notes or comments
    • Example: `meta: {notes: DC name}` or `meta: {notes: My cluster}`
  • failover — DNS Failover settings. The fields depend on the protocol you choose.
    •  TCP/UDP
  • port — the port to connect to. For example, 80, 443, or another one.
  • frequency — the interval of checks in seconds
  • timeout — the time within which your web servers should give the response in seconds
  • protocol — the protocol for connection
    •  ICMP
  • frequency — the interval of checks in seconds
  • protocol — the protocol for connection
  • timeout — the time within which your web servers should give the response in seconds
    •  HTTP
  • port — the port to connect to. For example, 80, 443, or another one.
  • frequency — the interval of checks in seconds
  • timeout — the time within which your web servers should give the response in seconds
  • protocol — the protocol for connection
  • host — the value of the Host header to be passed during the HTTP request
  • url — the URL that will be requested for checks
  • method — the method for checking the requests. For example, GET
  • tls — whether to use TLS. Can have either true or false value
  • http_status_code — the expected HTTP response code. Leave the field blank if any response is ok
  • regexp — the regular expression that should match the response body to make the check successful. Leave the field blank if the check is not needed
    • Example: `meta: {failover: {frequency: 10, port: 80, protocol: TCP, timeout: 10}}` or `meta: {failover: {frequency: 10, host: example.com, http_status_code: 500, method: GET, port: 80, protocol: HTTP, regexp: /folder/*, timeout: 10, tls: false, url: /failover}}`     ### Filters The following response selection filters can be applied to the resource records: ### 1. geodns The resource record will be included in the response if its metadata matches the geo data of the user's IP from the EDNS data or the recursor's IP. Example: `filters: [{type: geodns, strict: false}]` The following metadata is considered by the filter:
  • ip
  • asn
  • regions
  • countries
  • continents
  • default
  • notes
    •  ### 2. geodistance The resource records will be included in the response from nearest to furthest based on the distance from the user's IP to the coordinates specified in the metadata. Example: `filters: [{type: geodistance,strict: true}]` The following metadata is considered by the filter:
  • latlong
    •  ### 3. weighted_shuffle The resource records will be included in the response based on their weight value. The weight determines the frequency of the resource record getting into the selection. The default value is 50. Example: `filters: [{type: weighted_shuffle, strict: false}]` The following metadata is considered by the filter:
  • weight
    •  ### 4. default The resource records with `meta: {default: true}` are used by default when other records are not selected based on their meta. If the resource records have `meta: {default: false}` or don’t have this meta, and the filter has `strict: false`, then all records will be included in the response. No resource records will be returned if the filter has `strict: true`. Example: `filters: [{type: default, strict: true}]` The following metadata is considered by the filter:
  • default
    •  ### 5. first_n Cuts the first N resource records from the response (where N is the limit field value). Example: `filters: [{type: first_n, limit: 1}]` will return only one resource record. ### 6. is_healthy The resource records will be included in the response based on the results of the DNS Failover monitoring. Example: `filters: [{type: is_healthy, strict: false}]` The following metadata is considered by the filter:
  • backup

tags.name: Failover
tags.description:
DNS Failover is an option that monitors the availability of your domains or servers and, in case of issues, excludes non-working IP addresses from DNS responses. As a result, the traffic is redirected from the broken server to a working one, and your resource stays available for all users.

The option is paid. To activate it, contact the support team or your account manager.

post.description:
Imports a DNS zone into your account. To import the zone, add its contents in bind9 format like this: 

';TTL 14400
test.local. IN SOA     ns1.test.local. admin.test.local. (
2017082401      ; Serial
10800           ; Refresh
3600            ; Retry
604800          ; Expire
604800          ; Negative Cache TTL
)
IN      NS      ns1.test.local.
IN      NS      ns2.test.local.
IN      MX 10   mx.test.local.
IN      MX 20   mx2.test.local.
@               IN      A       192.168.1.1
localhost       IN      A       127.0.0.1
ns1             IN      A       192.168.1.2
ns2             IN      A       192.168.1.3
mx              IN      A       192.168.1.4
mail            IN      A       192.168.1.5
www             IN      CNAME   test.local.               '

APIKey.description:
To get access to our API, you need to have an account registered.
Sign up if you dont have one.

Most API requests require an API token which is a unique key that allows you to interact with our services. Additionally, it helps the API check if the user is allowed to perform the action.

Use a permanent API token for regular automated requests. You can set its validity period when creating it or issue a token for an unlimited time. Please address the API documentation of the specific product in order to check if it supports API tokens.

You can send only 5 requests per second.
To manage services, add your permanent API token after APIKey in the Authorization header.
'Authorization: APIKey eyJ0eXAiOiJKV'


Important! When authorizing via SAML SSO, be informed that our system does not have any information about permissions given to the user by the identity provider. Even if the provider revokes the user's access rights, their tokens remain active. Therefore, if necessary, the token will need to be deleted manually.
